entries.name: Extensive reading at coverage
entries.doesNotDo: It does not fix a word in memory. Words met while reading are met once; without the schedule picking them up they are gone in a week.

entries.name: Narrow reading
entries.trains: the same as extensive reading, faster, by reusing one topic's vocabulary
entries.doesNotDo: It broadens nothing. Four texts on one subject build that subject's vocabulary and leave the rest of the language exactly where it was.

entries.name: Intensive reading
entries.doesNotDo: It builds no volume. One paragraph exhaustively is the opposite of the input quantity fluency needs, and it cannot substitute for it.

entries.name: Reading aloud
entries.doesNotDo: It is not speaking. Every word is chosen for you, so it trains articulation and rhythm while leaving retrieval untouched.

entries.name: Reading and listening at once
entries.doesNotDo: It does not test listening. The text carries you, so it cannot tell you what you would have understood without it.

entries.name: Re-read something that was too hard
entries.trains: the competence moment — noticing that it got easier
entries.doesNotDo: It teaches almost nothing new. Its whole value is evidence of progress you can feel, which is a motivation effect and not a learning one.

entries.name: Parallel text
entries.doesNotDo: It removes the retrieval attempt. With the translation beside it, nothing forces you to work the meaning out, and unworked meaning does not stick.

entries.name: A book you already know in your own language
entries.doesNotDo: It lets you understand the story without understanding the sentences. Prior knowledge fills the gaps, so comprehension overstates what you read.
